claim: Current Sleep Score documents total sleep, efficiency, restfulness, REM, deep, latency, and timing as seven contributors.
limitations: Weights and complete formula not public

claim: Current documentation says staging uses movement, skin temperature, resting heart rate, HRV, and respiratory rate.
limitations: Aggregate agreement is not per-person accuracy; population details are on linked study

claim: At least three hours of stage detection in a 6pm-to-6pm sleep day are needed for a main sleep cycle; low battery may preserve interval data while losing stages and Readiness.
limitations: Operational documentation; not a validation study

claim: Oura acknowledges stillness may resemble sleep and movement or elevated heart rate may resemble wakefulness.
limitations: No error distribution provided

claim: A Gen3-era four-class algorithm study used 440 nights from 106 people in cross-validation.
limitations: Research algorithm/version may not equal current production; sponsor relationship needs inspection

claim: Oura underestimated total sleep and showed material stage biases in adolescents across restricted sleep opportunities.
source_title: Multi-Night Validation of a Sleep Tracking Ring in Adolescents
result: TST underestimated by roughly 33-47 minutes; stage-specific biases
limitations: Adolescents and older algorithm; laboratory sleep opportunities

claim: In healthy adults Oura Gen2 sleep/wake agreement was 89% with kappa 0.51.
source_title: A Validation of Six Wearable Devices
result: High sleep/wake agreement but moderate kappa
limitations: Older ring/algorithm and healthy laboratory cohort
conflicts_of_interest: Authors report device support relationships in paper

claim: Recent synthesis concludes total sleep estimates can be useful while stage classification remains moderately accurate.
source_title: The Oura Ring Versus Medical-Grade Sleep Studies
result: Overall sleep duration stronger than stages
limitations: Heterogeneous generations algorithms and populations

claim: Current Readiness documents nine contributors and describes personal averages learned over about two weeks with long-term generally two months.
limitations: Exact weighting/normalisation not public; metric-specific windows differ

claim: Current HRV Balance compares a 14-day weighted average with a three-month average.
limitations: Weighting and HRV artefact handling not public

claim: Current Recovery Index uses the timing of nightly lowest heart rate and describes six hours of sleep after that point as optimal.
limitations: No public causal validation or exact curve

claim: A historical Oura patent describes systems for assessing a readiness score from biological and activity signals.
limitations: A patent is neither current product specification nor clinical validation

claim: Current Activity Score documents stay active, move every hour, meet daily goals, training frequency, training volume, and recovery time.
limitations: Contains general guidance and proprietary score mapping

claim: Current guidance encourages one or two easy days weekly rather than maximal activity every day.
limitations: Exact personalisation and thresholds only partially documented

claim: Current app guidance says broad baselines usually require two to four weeks and displays not-enough-data states.
source_title: How to Use the Oura App
limitations: Conflicts with contributor-specific two-week and three-month windows; not one universal baseline

claim: Cycle Insights uses logged periods plus nighttime temperature trends; hormonal contraception hides phase/fertile-window outputs while retaining bleeding/symptom tracking.
limitations: Regional availability; marketing accuracy not a validation result

claim: Fertile Window 2.1 is intended to aid conception and explicitly is not contraception; performance specifies at least 70% fertile-day accuracy and ovulation forecast MAE up to three days.
limitations: Contraindicated/excluded contexts include hormonal contraception and limited irregular-cycle data

claim: A pending patent describes identifying phase morphology from multi-cycle temperature time series.
limitations: Not current product specification validation or permission to copy

claim: Current Pregnancy Insights is user-enabled and presents gestational context plus trends; new users need 7-14 days for baseline and significant temperature shifts may take 60-90 days to normalise.
limitations: Reference ranges are descriptive; not diagnosis

claim: A pending patent describes pregnancy detection from wearable physiological data.
limitations: LibreRing explicitly will not infer pregnancy; patent is not clinical validation

claim: Expert consensus concludes daily sleep timing regularity matters for health and performance.
result: Consensus supports regularity as a dimension
limitations: Association and consensus do not define an individual score curve

claim: AASM/SRS consensus recommends adults sleep seven or more hours regularly.
source_title: Recommended Amount of Sleep for a Healthy Adult
limitations: Individual needs vary; does not validate a wearable score

claim: WHO recommends adults undertake regular activity and generally 150-300 minutes moderate or 75-150 minutes vigorous weekly while limiting sedentary behaviour.
source_title: WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
limitations: Not a daily wearable-score target and must adapt for ability pregnancy and illness
